shared_elements: low-relief carving on weathered pale limestone blocks
horizontal register/band of repeated motifs running across the upper part
quadruped animal in profile with visible legs
repeated arched or curved motifs in a row
block set in situ among loose rubble and excavation debris
justification: Both surfaces are shallow, outline-style reliefs on rough limestone that divide the field into an upper horizontal band of repeated motifs (arches/hatching in B, a linear frieze in A) above a lower zone occupied by profile quadrupeds and elongated serpentine creatures, and both are photographed in situ among rubble, which strengthens the immediate impression of kinship. The clearest difference is density and legibility: A is crowded edge-to-edge with overlapping animal bodies filling the whole face, whereas B is sparser and more schematic, with large geometric arched forms and a prominent disc dominating over the few creatures, so the compositional scheme is only loosely, not specifically, shared.
